## Triage: first grade, `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `area:access` · `pm:queue` · triage seat · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-16T15:04Z

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Why p2:** a member without `setup.access` reaches Setup item pages by URL under another app's chrome, and a refused read is drawn as "No users assigned yet". The server still refuses the data.
- **Lane:** `domain:ui`. There are two landings, as the card says: the `/apps/setup/...` access verdict in `AppContent`, and `AssignedUsersSection.tsx`'s read-failure state (a refusal is not an empty list).

Claim: PM loop round 2
Session: `session_01Vk15bz8xHtKGUfXfCm16h4`
Account: `os-elon-musk` (the seat's linked user as `GET /user` answers it; the card's assignee)
Branch: `claude/issue-12706-setup-route-access`
Worktree: `objectui-issue-12706`
Domain: `domain:ui`
Seat: `domain:ui#3`
File surface: `packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx` (the app access verdict, so that every `/apps/APP/...` route a caller's app refuses draws `app-access-denied`, Setup's item routes included); the module that mounts Setup's metadata-admin routes, if the dev measures that the verdict must be read there (`packages/app-shell/src/console/setupApp.ts` is held by PR objectui#12662: serial, below); `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AssignedUsersSection.tsx` (the read-failure state only: a refused read is said as a refusal, as `PositionHoldersSection` does); tests beside each; one `.changeset/12706-*.md` (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (default tier; console routing with an access judgement per route; `dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui` over the named paths: no path-derived mandate)
Clause-②: no (no export, prop or type changes; the console draws its existing access-denied screen on more routes, and the section says "refused" instead of "empty")
Responsibility: `@object-ui/app-shell`'s console routing renders Setup's item pages for a caller the Setup app refuses (no `setup.access`), under another app's chrome, and `AssignedUsersSection` draws its refused read as "No users assigned yet" | the server refuses every read that matters (403), so nothing leaks; the console already owns the verdict screen (`app-access-denied`, objectui#4252), but these routes never reach it | any signed-in member who opens a Setup URL from a link or a bookmark, measured with a plain member on `main` `efa9cb4` and on PR #12685's build (the card's reproduction)
Thread-read: 6218383592
Serial constraints cleared: PR objectui#12731 (objectui#12715, another seat, ready) adds a named-record-page route to `AppContent.tsx` (+21); whichever lands second merges `main` and keeps both intents. PR objectui#12662 (objectui#12606, seat 4) changes `setupApp.ts`; this surface keeps out of it unless the dev measures that the verdict belongs there, and then this card lands after #12662. objectui#12285 (`pm:queue`, p3, the package-id probe in `AppContent.tsx`) is answered serial, not fold: gate ① fails, since #12285's defect is a probe that asks the by-name route with a package id and reads its 404 as not-found, a different shape and a different fix; it keeps its own `Restart-when`. `AssignedUsersSection.tsx` is free: PR #12685 landed as `fac2c24`. Read across the lane's `pm:dispatched` claims and every open objectui PR's file list, 2026-10-16T16:06Z.

**Scope correction on this card, by its filer** · `domain:ui` seat 3 · `session_01Vk15bz8xHtKGUfXfCm16h4` · 2026-10-16T17:17Z

The card's first "Expected" line said every `/apps/setup/...` route should draw the access verdict for a caller Setup refuses. Measurement falsified that wording (dev report `6220801711`, open question 1): members legitimately reach three routes under the Setup segment.
- `/apps/setup/system/approvals`: the server's approval `actionUrl` `/system/approvals`, forwarded by `SystemRedirect`.
- `/apps/setup/system/profile`.
- `/apps/setup/OBJECT/record/ID`: `ApprovalsInboxPage`'s `recordHref` falls back to `setup`.

A whole-subtree gate would cut those members off. So:
- **This card's scope, as PR #12739 lands it:** every page the reproduction measured, plus Setup's root.
  - the root `/apps/setup` (step 1);
  - the metadata-admin routes (steps 2–4: the lists, the permission-set and position editors);
  - the holders sections' refused read: `AssignedUsersSection`, and `PositionHoldersSection` after the claim's re-statement.
  - Each is verified in the browser by the dev on the PR's head.
- **Not carried, and not filed:** the rest of the Setup subtree for a refused caller: `component/…`, object lists, dashboards, and `system/*` other than approvals and profile.
  - It is read from code only. No producer links a member there, so it does not pass the filing gate today.
  - The dev's three shapes, A (stop here), B (a console allowlist) and C (move member-facing links off the Setup segment at their producers, then gate the subtree), are recorded in the PR's acceptance notes.
  - The seat rules on none of them. B would be a second access rule in the console, which this card's claim forbids. If a refused-caller page beyond these is ever measured, it is filed then, as a decision card, with these options.
